709932.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pā́wits. Cognates include Latin puer, Sanskrit पु॒त्र (putrá, “son”), and Avestan 𐬞𐬎𐬚𐬭𐬀 (puθra, “son”).

709995.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pərai, apparently from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂- (“before, in front”) and/or *per- (identical meaning), the details of which are disputed. Compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀞𐀫 (pa-ro).

709936.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *kʷelh₁-der.? Ancient Greek πάλαι (pálai) Ancient Greek -ος (-os) Ancient Greek παλαιός From πάλαι (pálai, “long ago”) + -ος (-os, “adjectival suffix”).

709935.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *kʷelh₁- (“far (in time or space)”).

709918.t: From παθ- (path-), zero-grade of the root of πάσχω (pắskhō, “to feel; to suffer”). Compare the aorist ἔπαθον (épathon).

709924.t: From παιδεύω (paideúō, “rear a child”) + -ία (-íā), from παῖς (paîs, “child”).

709972.t: Compound of πᾶν (pân, “everything”) + ἔργον (érgon, “work”) + -ος (-os, “noun of result or an abstract noun of action”).

709912.t: A nominalization of the verb πήγνυμι (pḗgnumi, “to stick, fasten, build, fix”), meaning "that what is built or fixed"; see also πάγη (págē, “snare, trap”) and Latin pagus.

709933.t: Derived from Proto-Indo-European *p(y)eh₂w- (“to hit, strike”). Cognates include Latin paviō.

709993.t: Reduplicated nursery word; compare πάππας (páppas, “daddy, papa”).

709901.t: From ὄψ (óps, “eye”) + -σις (-sĭs). Diachronically from Proto-Hellenic *ókʷtis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ékʷtis, from *h₃ekʷ- (“eye, to see”).

709968.t: From πάνοπλος (pánoplos, “in full armour”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā), from πᾶς (pâs, “all, every”) + ὅπλον (hóplon, “armour”).

709994.t: Unknown. Perhaps from Egyptian, since writing on it is widely believed to have originated in Egypt, but no Egyptian cognate is known.

709931.t: παῖς (paîs) + *-ϳω (*-jō), i.e. "to act like a child" > "to play".

709903.t: Nominal derivative from unattested *ὄψ (*óps), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁op-s, a derivative of *h₁epi (“on, near”); delicacies were considered side-dishes and were eaten on top of bread and such.

709942.t: Frozen adverbial accusative of *πάλις (*pális) from Proto-Indo-European *kʷl̥His, from *kʷel- (“to revolve”) (whence πέλω (pélō, “to go, be”) and πάλαι (pálai, “before, long ago”)).

709986.t: From παντο- (pănto-, combining form of πᾶς (pâs)) + κράτος (krắtos, “power; strength”) + -τωρ (-tōr, “agent-noun suffix”).

709943.t: The word may well be Pre-Greek, in view of the suffix "-ακ-".

709963.t: παν- (pan-) + ἄγυρις (águris), Aeolic form of ἀγορά (ăgorā́, “marketplace”)

709920.t: Uncertain; perhaps extracted from the expression ἰὴ παιήων, ἰὼ παιάν (iḕ paiḗōn, iṑ paián), an exclamation to begin songs, and/or ultimately from Pre-Greek.
